title: Brother, Will You Slight the Message
description: Brother, Will You Slight the Message in Tonic Solfa to ST. AUSTIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 511, “Calls of the Spirit”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.4.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AUSTIN; any other 8.7.8.7.4.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bro-ther, will you slight the mes-sage Sent in mer-cy from a-bove? Ev-ery sen-tence, O how ten-der, Ev-ery line how full of love! Heav-enly ac-cents Full of strength and peace and love!

lines: Brother, will you slight the message
Every line how full of love!
Full of strength and peace and love!
Tempted souls, they bring you succor;
Fearful hearts, they quell your fears;
Blessed he their word who hears!
Hasten to the court of heaven,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. AUSTIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
